newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo denounces U.N. "intimidation campaign".
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo denounces U.N. "intimidation campaign".

text.p: President Laurent Kabila's government denounced what it called a campaign of intimidation within the U.N. Security Council and rejected as defamatory suggestions of continuing massacres of refugees on its soil.

A cabinet statement, read by government spokesman and information minister Raphael Ghenda on state radio on Saturday, also unveiled economic measures ranging from road and hospital rebuilding to construction of a national fuel supply pipeline.

"The government vigorously denies the campaign of intimidation orchestrated within the Security Council against the so-called obstacles put in the way of humanitarian agencies' work in our territory by the government," he said.
"These so-called continuing massacres of refugees are defamatory and invented by those who failed to prevent the fall of the dictatorial regime in our country," he added.

Thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees have crossed into neighbouring Congo-Brazzaville, following the ousting of veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko by Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo after a seven-month civil war.
The U.N. refugee agency has flown home tens of thousands more in an airlift initiated after massacre reports.
The U.N. Security Council, alarmed by reports of massacres of refugees, called on Thursday for an immediate end to violence against the exiles in Kabila's Congo.
The refugees are remnants of more than one million Hutus who fled Rwanda in 1994 to escape reprisals for the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus.

The 15-member council called "in the strongest terms for complete cooperation with the U.N. mission investigating reports of massacres, other atrocities and violations of international law in the country".
Investigators have so far been refused access to suspected mass graves by Kabila's Tutsi-dominated army.
